Chapter 9: Navigating Setbacks and Returning to Calm
You know, even when you've built strong habits and started to shift your mindset, setbacks just happen. Stressful days, unexpected changes, or old triggers—they can sneak up and bring back that overthinking you thought you’d left behind. But here’s the thing: the goal isn’t to dodge every setback. It’s about how you respond—with patience, and maybe a little self-kindness.
When overthinking creeps back in, it’s so easy to get down on yourself, right? Maybe you feel discouraged, or you start judging yourself for slipping up. But what if—just for a moment—you saw these times as a chance to practice all those new skills you’ve been working on? Think of it like a musician who hits a wrong note. They don’t quit—they go back to their scales, their basics. And you can do the same. Whenever you need to, just return to your core practices—mindfulness, gratitude, whatever routines help you reset.
So, what are some gentle ways to handle setbacks?
First, try a self-compassionate check-in. When you notice you’re spiraling into overthinking, just pause for a second. Offer yourself a kind word—maybe something like, “It’s okay to feel this way. I can start again.” It’s amazing how much that simple kindness can help.
Next, revisit your tools. Maybe you have grounding techniques you like, or you keep a gratitude list handy. Even setting a timer to contain your worries can help break that cycle and give you some perspective.
And don’t forget about support. Sometimes, just reaching out to a friend, a mentor, or your community can make all the difference. Sharing what you’re going through—well, it can be enough to break the spell of rumination.
Picture this: you’ve been making real progress, feeling more at ease, and then suddenly, you’re stuck in a loop, worrying about some upcoming event. If you can notice the setback without beating yourself up, and gently return to your calming practices, you’ll bounce back faster—and probably with a lot less distress.
Here’s something to remember: setbacks are just part of growing. Every time you come back to your habits, you’re strengthening your ability to handle whatever life throws at you. Over time, you’ll find these setbacks happen less often—and when they do, they just don’t shake you like they used to. Instead, you’ll notice a steady sense of ease and resilience starting to take root.
